📌 Tehran, IRNA –Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi has presented a report on the latest diplomatic developments and consultations on regional and international issues, especially the recent quadrilateral summit between Iran, Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, and Turkiye.

Araghchi outlined the key points, including a quadrilateral summit between Iran, Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, and Turkiye, during a cabinet meeting that was chaired by President Masoud Pezeshkian on Wednesday.
​
The report detailed the discussions held during visits by a Qatari delegation, as well as the consultations involving Mohsen Rezaei, Secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council; Khalid bin Salman, Saudi Minister of Defense; Asim Munir, Chief of the Army Staff of Pakistan; and Ibrahim Kalin, Director of the National Intelligence Organization of Turkiye.
​
On the quadrilateral talks, the report said the importance of regional cooperation, the strengthening of joint security mechanisms, and the prevention of the escalation of tensions and conflicts were underscored.
​
Participants, it said, also warned against the consequences of the Israeli regime's deliberate policies—specifically its efforts aimed at weakening regional states, expanding the scope of its aggressions, laying the groundwork for the destabilization of governments, and drawing the United States into regional conflicts.
​
The senior officials of the four regional powers stressed the need for regional countries to remain vigilant against tension-inducing trends, and to strengthen cooperation to preserve sovereignty, stability and the territorial integrity of nations.
​
Furthermore, a report was also presented on Pezeshkian's recent visit to Russia, covering his bilateral meetings and discussions with foreign leaders on the sidelines of the 8th Summit of the Gas Exporting Countries Forum (GECF) in Moscow.
